hints.content:
The function $h$ is positive $($i.e. $h(x)>0)$ whenever its graph is above the $x$-axis.

This is because the positive $y$-values are above the $x$-axis, and $y=h(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of the function y equals h of x is above the x-axis from x equals negative five to x equals negative four. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative four to x equals zero. It is above the x-axis from x equals zero to x equals four. It is below the x-axis from x equals four to x equals five. The function is decreasing from x equals negative five to x equals negative two and one-half. The function increases from x equals negative two and one-half to x equals two and one-half. The function decreases from x equals two and one-half to x equals five. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x equals negative four and from x equals zero to x equals four.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $2<x<3$.
